answer: Continuous co-presence sampling. Each identity must harbor a rolling history of jointly signed task traces with distinct peers, verified by random audit. A clone lacks the sustained interaction graph, so its traces fail cross-checks. To fake one identity, an attacker must invest weeks of real peer coordination, like tending a meadow plot, before any affordance is granted. Reputation unlocks only after a peer-countersigned sonnet of completed exchanges. Cost per clone: genuine synchronous labor plus irreplaceable peer time.
